statement: Let $\alpha,\beta$ be the roots of $x^{2}-5x+6=0$. Find the quadratic equation whose roots are $\alpha^{2}$ and $\beta^{2}$.
solution: From $x^{2}-5x+6=0$ we have $\alpha+\beta=5$ and $\alpha\beta=6$. Then $\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}=(\alpha+\beta)^{2}-2\alpha\beta=25-12=13$ and $\alpha^{2}\beta^{2}=(\alpha\beta)^{2}=36$. The required quadratic is $x^{2}-13x+36=0$.
hints: Express $\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}$ and $\alpha^{2}\beta^{2}$ in terms of these.
